skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-new-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta bidding for first-time WooCommerce buyers with Product Metrics. Check tracking, verify first-order events, and choose a revenue or profit conversion in Meta.
skill.summary: Use first paid WooCommerce orders as the conversion signal for Meta new customer bidding.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or normal setup checks, not shell substitution or host reconnaissance. Real risks include agent access to order records, a broadly capable vendor interface, and an unpinned installer. The workflow also lacks clear approval for data sharing, allows direct handling of a Meta token, and cites the wrong profit event.

remediation.issue: The assistant can accept the Meta access token and pass it to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require the merchant to enter the token directly in the Product Metrics app. Do not collect it in chat or pass it through command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require approval before historical order import or live event sharing.
remediation.suggestion: Before each transfer, explain which data will go where. Ask the merchant to confirm the store, property, destination pixel, and consent settings before proceeding.

remediation.issue: The agent can query order details and execute vendor API operations.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only access for setup checks and request approval for writes. Limit order reads to the approved store and return classifications without unnecessary customer details.

remediation.issue: The profit guidance cites the general order-profit event instead of the first-order profit event.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT consistently. Verify the event and rule in Events Manager before the merchant changes the ad set.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the installer package or source revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin both to reviewed versions and make installation a separate step that requires the user's approval.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Access Token Can Enter Agent Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits the assistant to accept a Meta Conversions API token and pass it to a command. This may expose the token in chat history, tool records, or process arguments even if the assistant never repeats it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exception and conflicting app-entry guidance are explicit. Actual retention depends on the client and execution environment.

semantic_findings.title: Data Sharing Lacks an Explicit Approval Step
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can start when Product Metrics is not named and guides merchants through importing existing orders and enabling live Meta sending. It does not require separate approval of the historical import or explain the matching data before asking users to enable sending.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The import and send instructions are explicit, and both involve merchant UI actions. Shopper consent controls Meta delivery but does not replace merchant approval of the intended transfers.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Guidance Can Select the Wrong Bidding Signal
semantic_findings.description: The main skill recommends PMOrderProfit with ORDER_PROFIT, while the new customer guide requires PMNewCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_NEW_PROFIT. Using the general event can direct ad spend toward repeat buyers instead of first-time buyers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions specify two different event and rule pairs for the same goal. The merchant makes the final selection, so the spending impact is conditional.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta New Customer Bidding for WooCommerce
content.value_statement: A standard purchase conversion treats first-time and returning buyers alike. Use Product Metrics to send a separate first-order event and select it as your bidding signal in Meta.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify which WooCommerce or Meta steps remain.
Guide the store owner through plugin connection, paid order settings, consent setup, and Meta destination checks.
Review recent orders in the selected store and report which buyers are new, returning, or unknown.
Guide a first paid test order and check that the new customer event reaches Meta.
Explain how to create a first-order revenue or profit conversion in Meta and verify the ad set selection.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a connected WooCommerce store, and access to the relevant Meta pixel or dataset.
The merchant creates the custom conversion and selects the ad set event in Meta.
Profit events require complete contribution margin data. New customer classification depends on available paid order history.
Meta does not receive historical orders through this workflow or revise events after later refunds.

use_cases.title: Check store readiness
use_cases.description: Identify missing store, consent, and Meta tracking steps before placing a test order.

use_cases.title: Test an acquisition campaign signal
use_cases.description: Verify a first-order event and prepare the custom conversion for one Meta ad set.

use_cases.title: Explain unexpected order classifications
use_cases.description: Check whether paid statuses or guest email matching explain why recent orders were classified as returning or unknown.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting with an existing WooCommerce store
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Product Metrics setup for WooCommerce and Meta. Tell me what remains before I can test a first-order event. Do not change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent orders
prompt_templates.scenario: Checking customer classification before a test
prompt_templates.prompt: For my selected store, summarize the last 20 orders as new, returning, or unknown. Do not include customer names or email addresses.

prompt_templates.title: Verify first-order revenue
prompt_templates.scenario: Validating an event before changing an ad set
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a new guest test order with marketing and analytics consent. Help me verify PMNewCustomer in Meta before I select the conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a profit pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing first-order profit on one ad set
prompt_templates.prompt: Check margin coverage and whether PMNewCustomerProfit reached my Meta pixel with the correct purpose. Give me the steps to set up one ad set for the pilot.

output_examples.input: Is my store ready to test new customer bidding?
output: WooCommerce is connected and both webhooks are active.
The Meta destination is saved. A first paid test order is still needed.
Check that the test purchase has marketing and analytics consent. Verify that Meta receives the new customer event before creating the conversion.

output_examples.input: Why did my test order not send a new customer event?
output: The guest billing email matches an earlier paid order, so Product Metrics classified this buyer as returning.
Use a test email with no earlier paid orders and confirm the new order reaches a paid status.

output_examples.input: Which event should I use for first-order profit?
output: Use PMNewCustomerProfit with the new customer profit purpose. The general order-profit event includes orders outside this goal.
Verify the event in Meta Events Manager before selecting the custom conversion in your ad set.

best_practices: Confirm the store, property, Meta pixel, and consent settings before importing orders or enabling live delivery.
Enter the WooCommerce setup token in WordPress and the Meta access token in the Product Metrics app.
Verify the first paid test order in Events Manager, then remove the test code before checking live delivery.
anti_patterns: Using the standard purchase or general order-profit event when the goal is first-time buyers.
Counting unpaid, failed, or cancelled orders as paid to make a test pass.
Pasting setup tokens, access tokens, or raw customer records into chat.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics decide whether a customer is new?
faq.answer: It looks for earlier paid WooCommerce orders under the same customer account or guest billing email. Only your selected paid statuses count.

faq.question: What is the difference between the two new customer events?
faq.answer: PMNewCustomer carries first-order revenue. PMNewCustomerProfit carries first-order profit when margin data is complete.

faq.question: Why is the event missing from Meta Events Manager?
faq.answer: Meta must receive the event first. Check that the order is a first paid order and that the test has marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Who changes the conversion event in Meta?
faq.answer: You create the custom conversion in Events Manager and select it in the ad set. The assistant guides and verifies the setup.

faq.question: Are past orders sent to Meta or updated after a refund?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics does not backfill past orders to Meta, and later refunds do not revise events already sent.

faq.question: Where should I enter Meta and WooCommerce tokens?
faq.answer: Enter your Meta access token in the Product Metrics app and your WooCommerce setup token in WordPress Admin. Keep both out of chat.
